_doc: Anti-drift compass for the HIVE DEEPWALK EXPANSION arc (Ian 2026-07-27: 'I love this flow we just had in marketplace'). Companion to HIVE_DEEPWALK_EXPANSION_ROADMAP.md. tools/hive_deepwalk_scoreboard.py reads this and emits a MEASURED % per phase and per HK class. EXPANSION means growing BOTH denominators: journeys x personas x states (board 1) and new HK dimension classes (board 2). A cell moves only on cited live evidence.
_phases_def: ground - map the views, transitions and the caches each one touches
walk - live-MCP journey walk carrying the full lens; requires >=2 personas AND >=2 states
observe - record friction with evidence (a clean walk is a real result, record it as such)
harvest - Engine B, at spoke 5 ONLY, for a friction the walk actually surfaced
resolve - fix, then LOCK with a gate; a fix without a gate is not done
_coverage_rule: A journey's W phase is 'done' only when walked in >=2 personas AND >=2 states. One-persona/one-state is the shallowness this arc exists to kill.

H6-invite-and-code-lifecycle.notes: Code generation + regeneration. Does regenerating invalidate the old code immediately? | 2026-07-27 WALKED and found a REAL defect with a concrete human cost. The invite-code strip was filled ONLY from localStorage wh_hive_code, which is written by exactly two flows: creating the hive, or joining as a supervisor with the code already in hand. EVERY other route to being a supervisor leaves it empty - being PROMOTED by another supervisor, signing in on a new device, clearing storage, or returning through recoverHiveMembership (which rebuilds from the truth views and can only set the code `if (first.code)`, and the worker truth view does not carry it). VERIFIED LIVE: a supervisor with no cached code clicks 'Show Invite Code' and gets a panel reading 'Share this code with your team... Members enter this code to join your hive' with NO CODE IN IT. That is this arc's signature shape - a displayed claim with nothing behind it - and the consequence is not cosmetic: that supervisor CANNOT INVITE ANYONE. FIXED by asking the server, which can answer: v_hives_truth carries invite_code and is member-scoped. Fetch on demand when the cache is empty, cache it for next time, and on failure say 'Code unavailable - refresh to try again' rather than leaving an empty strip pretending to be a code. VERIFIED LIVE after the fix: real code GPU9XJ shown and matching the DB. TENANCY RE-VERIFIED for the new read, since it exposes a credential-ish value: from her session only her 2 hives are visible, a foreign hive's invite_code returns null, no error - RLS row-filtering, not an app-level check. INSTRUMENT NOTE (verify-the-instrument, twice in one journey): my first probe read btn-show-code as 'not visible' and I nearly filed that as the bug. It sits inside a COLLAPSED MENU (btn-hive-menu), so it was unrendered, not hidden - the same class of probe error as the position:fixed/offsetParent trap. Open the container before judging visibility.

H7-change-member-role.notes: hive_members.update. Does the demoted member's OPEN SESSION lose the affordances, or only after reload? | 2026-07-27 WALKED via the H8b thread, and it found the WORST defect of this arc so far. FOUND BY CHASING A WEAK TEST, not by walking: the revocation spec's marker assertion had no teeth for a seeded supervisor persona (after recovery they are a supervisor again, so 'marker present' is correct either way). Removing that persona dependency meant controlling the role directly, which exposed that the H8 fix only cleared html.is-supervisor on the KICKED branch - never on the ROLE SYNC branch two lines below it. DEFECT: demote a supervisor to worker and the role syncs correctly (wh_hive_role -> 'worker') while the paint marker stays. Worse than the revocation case because the board RENDERS for a demoted member, and the supervisor rules are FUNCTIONAL, not cosmetic: html.is-supervisor sets #my-work-card{display:none} and hides #pm-overdue-alert and #stock-alert (right for a supervisor, who gets the summary panel instead). VERIFIED LIVE on a real demotion: role 'worker', marker still true, and all three elements computed display:none - so a demoted worker lost their own work card AND their overdue-PM and stock alerts while the page otherwise looked completely normal. This is precisely the misapplication H8's own code comment predicted one commit earlier. FIXED with toggle() at the sync point, so promotion is covered by the same line - the mirrored bug would have left a freshly promoted supervisor on the worker layout until their next sign-in. VERIFIED BOTH DIRECTIONS LIVE: demote -> marker false, work card back (flex), PM alert back (block); promote -> marker true, supervisor layout back. W=partial and deliberately so: the role change was driven through the DB, so the SUPERVISOR-INITIATED UI path (the member list's role control) is still unwalked - that is what W=done would claim and it would not be true.

H8-remove-member.notes: hive_members.delete. THE REVOCATION QUESTION: what does P-removed still hold client-side and still render? Drive-order item 1. | 2026-07-27 WALKED as P-supervisor (performed the removal) then as P-removed (the member it happened to), across S-populated / S-stale / S-empty. THE GOOD NEWS FIRST: revocation itself is enforced in DATA, not chrome. Deleting the membership while her browser still held Lucena/supervisor state produced view-onboard, the board never rendered, and every supervisor-only numeric node came back unfilled - so the H8 answer to HK1's question is that the boundary held. THREE DEFECTS FOUND IN WHAT REVOCATION LEFT BEHIND: (1) html.is-supervisor SURVIVED the removal. It is set early from the CACHED role as a deliberate CLS optimisation, before the async membership check can finish, and nothing cleared it - a role marker outliving the role. Harmless today only because the board never renders for a removed member; the moment any supervisor-only rule keys off that class on a view a removed member CAN see, it misapplies. This is exactly HK1's recorded caveat shape. FIXED: the kicked branch removes the class. (2) THE BIGGER ONE - being removed from your ACTIVE hive dumped you to the create/join onboarding even while you were still a member elsewhere. The branch only ever considered the hive just lost. A worker in two plants, removed from one, was told to join or create a team. FIXED: state for the lost hive is cleared and the page reloads into recoverHiveMembership(), which re-queries and lands her in a hive she still belongs to. (3) FOUND WHILE VERIFYING (2), and the sharper bug: my first fix gated that reload on getHiveList() - a localStorage CACHE - so an empty or stale cache would still answer 'you have no hives' on the server's behalf. That is the identical cache-trust defect the marketplace arc fixed twice (role-gate on session, not cache). FIXED PROPERLY: the reload is unconditional; only the server may answer that question. And the mirror case - when the server DEFINITIVELY returns zero memberships, the cached list is now cleared, because the switcher renders straight from it and would otherwise offer 'Switch Hive (3)' naming hives she was removed from. Cleared only on a definitive empty answer, never on a query error, since a cache must not be dropped because the network blinked. VERIFIED LIVE, all three cases, on the real removal: A multi-hive -> lands on the Manila board as worker, is-supervisor gone; B empty cache + server has Manila -> recovers from the server and rebuilds the list (old code showed onboard); C zero memberships -> onboard, wh_hives '[]', switcher hidden, and navigation type 'reload' recorded EXACTLY ONCE, which is the no-loop proof the unconditional reload needed. Test DB restored to its pre-walk state and the multi-hive fixture my own walk consumed was put back (see HK2). | 2026-07-27 H8b FOLLOW-ON: the fix committed in a7167f1 was INCOMPLETE. It cleared the marker on the kicked branch only; the role-sync branch directly below it had the same defect with a bigger blast radius (see H7). The lesson is about scope, not vigilance: I fixed the path I had WALKED rather than every path that mutates the thing I was fixing. A marker set from cache must be reconciled wherever the truth arrives, and there were two such places. | 2026-07-27 H8 HARVEST: retrieve-first night_crawler query on the revocation friction returned the multitenant rule that exposed the switch-path defect (see H10 / H8d). The harvest spoke is cheap when it is aimed at OBSERVED friction and queried before crawling - 0 crawl tokens, one real bug.

So the clear-then- adopt sequence (applyHiveRole('') in leaveHive, then applyHiveRole(membership.role) in renderHiveSwitcher off a SERVER-verified role) holds. H10-switch-hive.notes: WAS UNWALKABLE BY CONSTRUCTION until 2026-07-27 (see HK2): seeded data was strictly 1:1 worker->hive so the switcher list was always length 1. Seeder now creates one P-multi worker with a DIFFERENT role in the second hive, so the switch is observable. R=partial: the fixture is fixed, the walk is owed. Drive-order item 1. | 2026-07-27 WALKED (first walk of this arc, and it found a real defect). FIXTURE: gave christinedizon a 2nd membership (Lucena Pharmaceutical, role supervisor) alongside Manila Electronics (worker) - the same shape the seeder now produces, so local state matches a post-reseed world. DEFECT FOUND: the switcher listed only ONE hive while the DB had two. Root cause is precise - the if(HIVE_ID) branch re-validates the ACTIVE membership every load (syncs role, clears everything on kicked) but never refreshes the LIST; wh_hives is written at sign-in (index.html) and rebuilt only by recoverHiveMembership(), which runs SOLELY when the user has no active hive. So a membership granted after sign-in - a supervisor adding you to a second plant, a join on another device - stayed invisible until sign-out. Same shape as the identity caches that bit this platform twice: trusted when present, re-derived only when absent. FIXED: reconcileHiveList() now runs on every board load (one bounded query against v_worker_truth + v_hives_truth, the same views the recovery path uses; best-effort so it never blocks the board; preserves any invite code already held since the truth view does not carry it). VERIFIED LIVE end to end: both hives now listed with correct per-hive roles, active hive unchanged (no disruption), and the SWITCH itself re-derives all three caches together - id b4f7fe63->4eec150e, name Manila->Lucena, and critically role worker->supervisor rather than carrying the old role across. | 2026-07-27 H8d — THE FLYWHEEL'S HARVEST SPOKE ACTUALLY PAID OFF, which is worth recording because it is the first time in this arc that Engine B drove Engine A rather than the reverse. Ran the harvest RETRIEVE-FIRST (night_crawler --query, 0 crawl tokens) on the friction H8/H8b surfaced: 'what does a user see when their role is revoked'. The bag already held the governing rule, in skill_multitenant-engineer: 'Hive Switch Must DB-Validate Membership Before Loading Board - trusting localStorage alone allows kicked workers to re-enter their old hive on the next auto-switch.' No crawl was needed; the retrieval pointed straight at switchToHive(), which I had read earlier and not questioned. IT VIOLATED THE RULE ON BOTH COUNTS. (1) It adopted the role from the CACHED wh_hives entry and called initBoard() with NO server check - the same cache-answers-for-the-server mistake as the kicked branch, so a stale list let a removed worker walk back into the board shell of a hive they no longer belong to (RLS still starved it of data, so it reads as a broken app rather than a revoked membership). (2) It never reconciled html.is-supervisor, because a switch does not RELOAD - it calls initBoard() in place, so the H8b page-load fix never ran. VERIFIED LIVE BEFORE FIXING: switching from her supervisor hive into the hive where she is a WORKER left marker=true and #my-work-card at display:none. Third door onto the same defect, and the exact lesson I had written one commit earlier - fix every path that mutates, not only the one you walked. FIXED: the switch now queries v_worker_truth for that hive, uses the SERVER's role rather than the remembered one, toggles the marker to match, writes the corrected role back into the cached list so the next paint-from-cache starts from truth, and on a non-member refuses the switch, drops the stale entry from the switcher and says why. VERIFIED LIVE, all three outcomes: supervisor->worker switch repaints (marker false, work card flex); role taken from server even when the cached entry deliberately said 'supervisor'; switching into Baguio Textile Mills (never a member) refused, list 3->2, active hive unchanged, toast "You're no longer a member of Baguio Textile Mills." LOCKED by a 4th test in journey-hive-revocation.spec.ts.

H14-cross-surface-hive-identity.notes: A switch or removal must be correct on EVERY page reading whHiveId(), not just the board that changed it. Cache set grounded 2026-07-27: wh_hive_id, wh_hive_name, wh_hive_role, wh_active_hive_id, wh_hives, wh_hive_lastseen_<id>. Drive-order item 1. | 2026-07-27 H8c CROSS-SURFACE SWEEP (the H8b lesson generalised: a marker painted from cache must be reconciled wherever the truth arrives, so WHICH OTHER surfaces gate on a cached role?). Swept every reader of wh_hive_role (69 refs / 29 files) and went straight at the canonical one, wh-roles.js, on the theory that if the SSOT trusts the cache then every page inherits it. Found something different and worse than staleness: a VOCABULARY MISMATCH. The reader reads the AUTH key (wh_hive_role, holding what hive_members.role holds) while its capability map mirrors nav-hub's `roles` arrays, written in DISPLAY vocabulary (field|supervisor|engineer). hive_members.role stores 'worker'. 'worker' was not in ROLES, so whRole() returned '' - and '' is DELIBERATELY permissive ('solo mode / new install', so a lone tech is not locked out). Two reasonable decisions composing into an unreasonable outcome: CONFIRMED IN THE BROWSER that with wh_hive_role='worker' the reader returned '' and can('approve') / can('manage_hive') / can('audit_log') ALL returned true - for 12 of 16 seeded memberships, i.e. every real worker. SEVERITY, stated honestly: NOT a privilege escalation. isSupervisor() was always correct for 'worker', the server remains the authority via RLS (the file's own security note), and crucially can() has ZERO production callers today - every WHRoles reference in the codebase is a COMMENT telling the next change to use it. So this shipped harmless by accident while sitting one call away from real. FIXED by mirroring nav-hub's existing worker->field mapping rather than inventing a second vocabulary (nav-hub's _defaultMode already does exactly this). VERIFIED LIVE after the fix: 'worker' -> role 'field', can_approve false, can_manage_hive false, can_logbook still true. GATED: tools/validate_role_vocabulary_coverage.py compares the reader's vocabulary against LIVE distinct hive_members.role values - live rows because the failure was a mismatch between what the DB WRITES and what the client UNDERSTANDS, so reading source alone would compare the client against itself. Instrument verified: FAILS on the pre-fix reader, passes on the fix, and catches a hypothetical future role in the selftest. A SECOND, non-code finding worth keeping: wh-roles.js is loaded platform-wide (nav-hub loads it, sw.js caches it) and called by nothing - a claimed centralization that centralizes nothing yet. Left in place and CORRECT rather than deleted, since the roadmap's +RBAC axis wants it adopted; but 'the SSOT exists' is not the same claim as 'the SSOT is used', which is the marketplace arc's lesson in a new costume.

HK1-boundary-is-real-not-cosmetic.seed: A role/tenancy boundary must be enforced by DATA (RLS or a server-derived role), never by CSS visibility alone. A hidden element must be EMPTY, not display:none over real data.
HK1-boundary-is-real-not-cosmetic.notes: 2026-07-27 SWEEP (partial, one page): hive.html PASSES with a caveat. #supervisor-summary is present in a worker's DOM (9,699 chars) behind class='hidden', but contains TEMPLATE ONLY - zero filled numeric nodes. Then the stronger probe: forging wh_hive_role to 'supervisor' in localStorage and reloading, the page OVERWROTE it back to 'worker' and granted nothing, so the role is server-re-derived. That is the opposite of the marketplace's wh_last_worker/wh_hive_id staleness. CAVEAT driving the detect stage: the pattern is fragile - if a later change fills that panel before checking role, CSS becomes the only thing hiding real data. | 2026-07-27 CONFIRMED BOTH WAYS on the same user across a hive switch, which settles the caveat: as a WORKER the panel is hidden AND contains zero filled values; as a SUPERVISOR it is visible AND filled (20/4/0/65). The data is therefore fetched CONDITIONALLY ON ROLE, not fetched-then-hidden - CSS was never the gate here. Combined with the forged-role probe (wh_hive_role set to supervisor is overwritten back to worker on load, because the if(HIVE_ID) branch re-validates against v_worker_truth), hive.html's role boundary is real on both the data and the identity side. detect/gate still owed: a detector that asserts this stays true, since the failure mode is a future change that fills the panel before checking. | 2026-07-27 H8 CLOSES THE CAVEAT'S FIRST HALF: the fragile pattern was real but inverted from what I expected. The panel stayed empty; it was the html.is-supervisor PAINT HINT that outlived the role, set from cache before the server check completes. Now cleared on revocation. The class's detect stage is therefore two assertions, not one: (a) a hidden element must be empty, and (b) a role marker must not survive the role. | 2026-07-27 DETECT+GATE BUILT, deliberately as TWO instruments because the class makes two different kinds of claim. (a) STATIC: tools/validate_role_marker_revocation.py - a role-derived class on a persistent root (<html>/<body>) must be removable somewhere in the same file. Verified as an instrument rather than assumed: run against the PRE-fix hive.html it FAILS on 'is-supervisor', against the fix it passes. Narrow on purpose (root targets only, role-vocabulary names only, toggle() counts as removal) so a PASS is not diluted; button-lock's 'is-loading' is pinned as a selftest false-positive. Registered in run_platform_checks (Platform) and PASSED in a full harness run. (b) LIVE: tests/journey-hive-revocation.spec.ts - 3 tests covering what static analysis cannot see, namely whether the removal actually RUNS on the revocation and demotion paths, plus the hidden-panel-must-be-empty assertion. Teeth verified by reverting the fix: the demotion test FAILS without it. HK2-testability-of-a-built-capability.seed: If the product ships a capability, seeded state must be able to EXERCISE it. A capability no fixture can reach is untested by construction, and its bugs are invisible to every walk and every screenshot.
HK2-testability-of-a-built-capability.notes: 2026-07-27 FOUND + FIXED: seeded data was strictly 1:1 worker->hive (15 memberships / 15 workers / 0 multi-hive) because hives_workers.py built exactly one member_row per worker, while hive.html carries ~28 hive-switcher references. H10 was therefore unwalkable by construction. Fixed in the seeder: one worker now receives a second membership in a different hive with a DIFFERENT role, so the switch is observable rather than merely possible. Same lesson as the marketplace trust columns in a new shape - the SEEDER decides what can be tested; under-generating a relationship is the quieter failure because nothing looks wrong. GATE owed: assert every shipped capability has a fixture that can reach it. | 2026-07-27 H8 PROVED THIS CLASS ON ITSELF: walking the removal DELETED the platform's only multi-hive membership, so H10's switch journey silently became unwalkable again - the fixture regression this class exists to catch, caused by a walk rather than a seeder. Restored the membership to match what the seeder now produces. The gate stage should therefore assert live fixture COVERAGE (>=1 multi-hive worker exists), not merely that the seeder contains the code to create one. | 2026-07-27 GATE BUILT: tools/validate_fixture_capability_coverage.py asserts LIVE ROWS can reach each capability (a 2+-hive worker for the switcher; both a supervisor and a non-supervisor for any role-boundary diff; a 2+-member hive for the member-list/remove flows). Live rows, NOT seeder source, precisely because the H8 walk deleted the only multi-hive membership while the seeder still contained the code to create one - a seeder-reading gate would have reported PASS with the fixture gone. A failed query counts as a shortfall, never a silent pass, since 'I could not tell' must not read as 'covered'. Skips clean when the DB is down (fixture check, not uptime). Selftest pins the exact H8 regression shape. Registered in run_platform_checks (Platform, skip_if_fast).

HK3-role-change-repaints-every-surface.seed: Adopting a role is not one assignment: it is the module variable, the stored hint, and every surface painted from it, and those must move together. A value with invariants attached needs ONE adopter, so the invariant is written once instead of remembered at each call site.
